acceptance_checks: evaluate_lock_grant returns satisfied for a task whose locks list is EMPTY — the vacuity case, asserted explicitly and documented in the docstring.
A task with an active lock record covering every declared lock dispatches exactly as today.
A missing lock record refuses the dispatch, and the reason names the task and the declared locks.
A record whose state is not active refuses.
A record covering only some declared locks refuses and names the uncovered ones.
An unreadable or malformed record refuses.
dispatchable_task_ids excludes any task the dispatcher would refuse — the two use the same predicate.
cmd_task_status refuses to move an ungranted task into ready, with the same reason, and succeeds once granted.
Neither dispatch nor a status change ever acquires a lock as a side effect.
The measured 2026-08-04 sequence — conflicted lock acquire, then dispatch — is refused with a reason naming the conflicting task.
tests/test_lock_lifecycle.py's cmd_dispatch_check driver agrees with the new predicate.
scripts/test_shiki_runner_claude.sh, test_shiki_daemon_runner.sh, test_shiki_loop_lock_guard.sh, test_shiki_control_plane.sh and test_shiki_goal_loop.sh all pass unchanged.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.
non_goals: A merge-side lock-grant requirement in mergegate_check.py
Changing what a lock conflict means, or how locks are declared or released
Adding a shiki lock release command
Auto-acquiring locks as a side effect of dispatch or of a status change
Touching any file outside the declared locks
scope:
Add a shared predicate — `evaluate_lock_grant(target, task)` in `scripts/shiki_tasks.py` — returning whether the task's declared locks are currently granted to IT, plus a reason when they are not. Semantics, stated explicitly in the docstring:
  - a task whose `locks` list is EMPTY has nothing to grant and is SATISFIED (vacuously). Treating an empty list as ungranted would block every lock-free task;
  - a task that declares locks is satisfied only when `.shiki/locks/<task_id>.json` exists, is readable, has `state: active`, and its `locks` cover every path the task declares;
  - anything else — file missing, unreadable, `state` not active, or a declared lock absent from the record — is NOT satisfied, and the reason names the task and the specific missing or stale locks.

Enforce it in `scripts/shiki_runtime.py` beside the existing status check in `dispatch_runner_task` (`:522-526`): a task that is not satisfied is refused with that reason, in the same style as the existing refusals. `shiki_runtime.py` already imports from `shiki_tasks`, so no import cycle is introduced. Make `dispatchable_task_ids` (`:291-310`) and the `cmd_runner_execute` status write (`:299`) agree with the same predicate, so a task the dispatcher would refuse is not advertised as dispatchable.

In `scripts/shiki_tasks.py`, make the failure impossible to miss at its source: `cmd_lock_acquire` (`:946`) must keep returning non-zero on conflict AND must make the ungranted state legible to the next step; and `cmd_task_status` (`:1164`), which today writes `status = "ready"` with no lock check, must refuse to move a task INTO `ready` when its declared locks are not granted — naming the same reason. Do not auto-acquire: dispatch and status must REFUSE, never grant.

Add `tests/test_dispatch_lock_precondition.py` driving the real functions: a task with an active, covering lock record dispatches; the record missing refuses and the reason names the task and the locks; `state` not active refuses; a record that covers only SOME declared locks refuses and names the uncovered ones; an unreadable/malformed record refuses; a task with an empty `locks` list dispatches (the vacuity case, asserted explicitly); `dispatchable_task_ids` excludes a task the dispatcher would refuse; `cmd_task_status --status ready` refuses for an ungranted task and succeeds once granted; and a conflicted `lock acquire` followed by a dispatch attempt is refused — the exact sequence measured on 2026-08-04. Extend `tests/test_lock_lifecycle.py` where it drives `cmd_dispatch_check` (`:287`) so the two cannot drift.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: a task is dispatched, implemented, reviewed and merged while its lock grant does not exist. The only visible signal appears at the very end, as a closeout that unexpectedly demands a Guardian approval — because the ADR 0017 bookkeeping exemption requires the lock to move `active -> released`, and there is no lock to move. The cause is three steps upstream and nothing points at it.
  Reproduced live 2026-08-04: `shiki lock acquire` was piped through `tail -1`; the visible output was the closing brace, and `"locks_granted": false` with five conflict reasons — naming a superseded task that still held the paths — scrolled past. `shiki handoff task`, `shiki task status --status ready` and `shiki runner claude` all proceeded.
  Root cause, verified by reading: `cmd_lock_acquire` (`scripts/shiki_tasks.py:946`) returns 1 at the conflict branch BEFORE `write_json(lock_file, record)` (`:966`) and before the status write (`:982`), so nothing is recorded. `dispatch_runner_task` (`scripts/shiki_runtime.py:512-530`) checks runtime, status, tooling, auth, handoff, worktree and lease — and never reads `.shiki/locks/`. `cmd_task_status` (`:1164`) writes `ready` with no lock check.
  Why dispatch-side only: requiring a lock grant at MERGE time would retroactively block reopened work — `origin/main` holds exactly one active lock record for twelve non-terminal tasks — and would pull `scripts/mergegate_check.py` plus four shell fixture files into the change.
  Failure direction matters: a wrong predicate refuses every dispatch and stops all autonomous work, which is worse than the defect. Hence the explicit vacuity rule for empty `locks`, and reasons that always name the task and the specific locks.
  Reproducible when: the 2026-08-04 sequence — conflicted acquire, then dispatch — is refused with a reason naming the conflicting task, and a task with an empty locks list still dispatches.
test_command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && bash scripts/test_shiki_runner_claude.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_daemon_runner.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_loop_lock_guard.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .
title: Make a granted lock a precondition of dispatch
